name_note: The species was reclassified from Eubacterium hadrum, so older papers use that name.

sentences.text: Anaerostipes hadrus is an anaerobic colonic bacterium reclassified from Eubacterium hadrum and reported among the ten most abundant phylotypes in adult human faeces.
The strains that define it were isolated as d-lactate-utilizing bacteria from the faeces of a healthy person.
Reviews place the genus Anaerostipes among the butyrate producers of the Clostridium cluster of Firmicutes, which use butyryl-CoA:acetate CoA-transferase and butyrate kinase routes.
In one mouse experiment, adding the butyrate-producing strain BPB5 significantly aggravated chemically induced colitis.
